In [[mathematics]], specifically [[algebraic geometry]], the '''étale spectrum''' of a [[commutative ring]] or of an [[E-infinity ring|'''E'''<sub>∞</sub>]]-ring, denoted by Spec<sup>ét</sup> or Spét, is an analog of the [[prime spectrum]] Spec of a commutative ring that is obtained by replacing the [[Zariski topology]] with the [[étale topology]]. 

The usual prime spectrum Spec enjoys the following relation: for a [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]] (''S'', ''O''<sub>''S''</sub>) and a commutative ring ''A'',
:<math>\operatorname{Hom}(S, \operatorname{Spec}(A)) \simeq \operatorname{Hom}(A, \Gamma(S, \mathcal{O}_S))</math>,
where Hom on the left is for [[morphism of schemes|morphisms of schemes]] and Hom on the right [[ring homomorphism]]s. That is, Spec is the [[right adjoint]] to the [[global section]] [[functor]] <math>(S, \mathcal{O}_S) \mapsto \Gamma(S, \mathcal{O}_S)</math>. So, roughly, one can (and typically does) simply define the étale spectrum Spét to be the right adjoint to the global section functor on the category of "spaces" with étale topology.{{sfnp|Lurie|2018|loc=remark 1.2.3.6.}}{{sfnp|Lurie|2018|loc=remark 1.4.2.7.}}

Over a [[field of characteristic zero]], Behrend constructs the étale spectrum of a [[graded algebra]] called a perfect resolving algebra.{{sfnp|Behrend|2002}} He then defines a [[differential graded scheme]] (a type of a [[derived scheme]]) as one that is étale-locally such an étale spectrum.

The notion makes sense in the usual algebraic geometry but appears more frequently in the context of [[derived algebraic geometry]].
